## Install and inspect the suite

`phenoloom` brings together the **CTTIR Spatial Biology Suite**. Its four
required dependencies support segmentation, validated cell tables, reviewed
phenotyping, and spatial analysis. Each member keeps its own analysis API.

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("CTTIR/phenoloom", dependencies = NA)
```

List the suite members without attaching their packages:

```{r membership}
phenoloom::phenoloom_packages()
```

Inspect their versions in the current R library paths:

```{r status}
phenoloom::phenoloom_status()
```

The report reads installation metadata. It does not start external engines or
test whether a specific analysis workflow is supported. Where several copies
of a package exist, the first library in `.libPaths()` takes priority.

## Choose the member for each step

| Step | Package | Responsibility |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Segment tissue images | `segmantR` | Segmentation methods and review workflows |
| Prepare cell tables | `cellspecR` | Imports, schema validation, and verifiable storage |
| Assign phenotypes | `gatekeepR` | Marker gating and reviewed cell-type calls |
| Analyze spatial patterns | `phenoscapR` | Spatial statistics and visualizations |

Use each member's documented data contracts when transferring results between
steps. Installing the suite does not establish that an arbitrary set of image
exports and marker panels is compatible across all steps.

For interactive work, `library(phenoloom)` attaches all four members. For
scripts, explicit `package::function()` calls make function ownership clear
and avoid ambiguity when packages export the same name.

```{r help, eval=FALSE}
library(phenoloom)
help(package = "segmantR")
help(package = "cellspecR")
help(package = "gatekeepR")
help(package = "phenoscapR")
```

## Record the environment

Save the installed-version report together with the full session information
alongside analysis outputs:

```{r provenance, eval=FALSE}
environment <- list(
  suite = phenoloom::phenoloom_status(),
  session = utils::sessionInfo()
)
saveRDS(environment, "phenoloom-environment.rds")
```

This records installed versions; it is not a lockfile or a guarantee that the
same versions remain available. Use your project's environment-management
workflow to preserve exact dependencies when reproducing an analysis.

## External engines and licensing

Optional Cellpose, StarDist, and Mesmer engines are configured through
`segmantR`. The metapackage does not create Python environments or download
model weights. Follow the member's installation guide for required compilers,
system libraries, and engine-specific setup.

`phenoloom` is MIT licensed. Member packages, external engines, and model
weights keep their own licenses. Cite the packages and methods actually used
in the analysis.
